Only for the connection to your server, never for updates. Risk: an authority installed by a user – for example by your employer or by malware – can issue certificates for any server and so read the traffic. Only turn this on if you installed the authority yourself for your server.

The app will then also accept certificates for your server that were issued by a certificate authority a user installed.

Such an authority may come from your employer, a network administrator or malware. Whoever controls it can read and change the traffic, including your password and sign-in token. The only remaining protection is comparing the fingerprint with the web app.

Updates from GitHub are still checked against the system authorities only.

This is the first encrypted connection to %1$s. The easiest way to set it up is the QR code from the web app (Settings). If no QR code is possible: the fingerprint is an ID that belongs to this server. Compare it character by character with the one the web app shows under Settings → Server certificate. Only after your yes does the app remember it, and from then on it accepts only certificates that match it.

The app cannot check who %1$s is: the server issued its certificate itself, or your own authority did. That is normal for a server at home, but it could also be someone in between.

The easiest way is to scan the QR code from the web app (Settings). If no QR code is possible, do this:
1. Open the web app on a computer.
2. Go to Settings → Server certificate.
3. Copy the last 24 characters of the fingerprint into the field below.

The fingerprint is an ID that belongs to this server. If it matches, it is your server. This screen only shows its beginning.

%1$s shows a different certificate than the one you confirmed. That happens when the server gets a new key – or when someone is listening in between. Nothing has been sent. Only accept it if you changed the server yourself: the new fingerprint is shown only by the web app (Settings → Server certificate); copy its last 24 characters from there.
